meta.title: PKM System Prompt — Engineering Projects
meta.subtitle: PARA Framework for the Agent Engineering Era

report_card.summary: A complete system prompt and operating framework that turns every engineering git repo into a live node in a larger knowledge garden. Agents are instructed to dual-track code work and PKM enrichment using an evolved PARA model, frontmatter standards, WikiLinks, and mandatory crystallization — ensuring the knowledge surface compounds with every run.

story.title: The Seed Drop
story.narration: The PKM Engineering System Prompt is dropped into a git repo as CLAUDE.md. The agent is given two explicit tracks: ship code and enrich the project's PKM structure. Every change becomes raw material for the knowledge garden.

story.title: PARA Re-understood
story.narration: The classic PARA is updated for agents. Pipelines are bounded runs that must crystallize. Areas are judged by the callable skill surfaces they expose. Resources become active Skill Surfaces. Archive becomes Crystallized — invocable, not dormant.

story.title: Frontmatter & WikiLinks Enforced
story.narration: Every note must carry structured frontmatter (layer, maturity, para) and at least two meaningful WikiLinks. Isolated nodes are declared invisible. The graph begins to form.

story.title: Dual-Track in Action
story.narration: While building features or running experiments, the agent simultaneously creates Pipeline notes, decision records, and pattern docs. The prompt makes PKM work inseparable from engineering work.

story.title: Crystallization Gate
story.narration: When a pipeline closes, crystallization is mandatory. What was built, learned, and made reusable is written down and moved to Crystallized. The parent Area README is updated. Knowledge compounds.

story.title: Surface Expansion
story.narration: Each agent run leaves behind more callable context. The next run — whether by the same agent next week or a future collaborator — starts from a richer surface and therefore reaches further, faster, and deeper.

story.title: Vault Integration
story.narration: Git repos become L1/L2 instances inside the root eBrain vault. Skill Surfaces live in Resources. Crystallized knowledge is permanently invocable. kaaroViewer can render the living graph.

story.title: The Compounding Loop
story.narration: The loop is closed: better prompts → richer surfaces → more powerful agents → even better prompts. The engineering project stops being a collection of files and becomes a living, queryable node in the larger garden.

insights.title: Dual-track is the only sustainable engineering posture in the agent era
insights.body: Treating PKM enrichment as a separate 'documentation task' fails. The prompt makes it a co-equal track with shipping code. Every commit, decision, and experiment is forced to leave structured, linkable residue.

insights.title: Skill Surfaces turn passive resources into agent leverage
insights.body: By renaming Resources → Skill Surfaces and demanding they be callable and composable, the framework converts documentation from something agents read into something agents can invoke. This is the key multiplier.

insights.title: Crystallization prevents knowledge evaporation
insights.body: Without the mandatory crystallization step at pipeline close, valuable context disappears into chat history or commit messages. The prompt makes crystallization a first-class gate, turning transient work into permanent, invocable assets.

insights.title: WikiLinks + frontmatter create the substrate for kaaroViewer graphs
insights.body: The structural rules (≥2 links, typed frontmatter, maturity/layer taxonomy) are exactly what kaaroViewer needs to render live, navigable intelligence briefs. The prompt is pre-optimized for visualization.

insights.title: eBrain mapping turns every repo into a first-class garden citizen
insights.body: By explicitly mapping git repo activity to eBrain folders (Pipelines, Skill Surfaces, Areas, Crystallized), the framework makes every engineering project a live, queryable part of the larger personal knowledge garden rather than an isolated silo.

nodes.label: PARA Framework (Agent Engineering Era)
nodes.description: Updated PARA model (Pipelines, Areas, Resources→Skill Surfaces, Archive→Crystallized) designed so agents can maintain and compound personal knowledge alongside code work.

nodes.label: PKM Engineering System Prompt
nodes.description: The master CLAUDE.md template that gives agents explicit dual-track instructions and the full PARA operating system for engineering projects.

nodes.label: Pipelines
nodes.description: Bounded runs with a goal — feature sprints, experiments, agent jobs. They create context that must be crystallized into Skills or Area notes when closed.

nodes.label: Areas
nodes.description: Long-term responsibilities. In the Agent Era judged primarily by the quality and callability of the skill surfaces they expose.

nodes.label: Skill Surfaces
nodes.description: Formerly passive Resources. Now active, encoded, composable, and callable knowledge that lets agents run further, faster, and deeper.

nodes.label: Crystallized Archive
nodes.description: Formerly inactive Archive. Now a living store of cleanly encoded past decisions and learnings that future agents or humans can invoke without re-deriving.

nodes.label: Note Frontmatter Standard
nodes.description: Mandatory YAML frontmatter (published, title, tags, description, date, layer, maturity, para) that makes every note searchable, typed, and graph-ready.

nodes.label: WikiLinks Graph Building
nodes.description: Mandatory practice: every note must contain at least two meaningful WikiLinks. Isolated nodes (zero links) are declared invisible to the garden.

nodes.label: Pipeline Crystallization
nodes.description: Mandatory closing ritual for every pipeline: write what was built, learned, and made reusable, then move it to Crystallized and update the parent Area.

nodes.label: Knowledge Surface
nodes.description: The expanding, queryable surface area created by every agent run. The richer the surface, the more powerful and far-reaching the next run becomes.

nodes.label: eBrain Vault
nodes.description: Root PARA knowledge garden. Git repositories are treated as L1/L2 instances inside it, with clear folder-to-PARA mappings.

nodes.label: Dual-Track Workflow
nodes.description: The core operating mode: every engineering action (code, decision, experiment) is simultaneously a PKM enrichment action. The two tracks are inseparable.

nodes.label: kaaroViewer
nodes.description: The real-time knowledge graph viewer that can render the living library produced by this prompt and the broader garden.

nodes.label: Agent-Field
nodes.description: The underlying Agent/Skill/Context model that this entire PKM framework is built upon.

nodes.label: Compute Theory
nodes.description: The deeper compute and systems philosophy referenced by the framework.

nodes.label: ego-Field
nodes.description: The area-of-effect concept that describes how a system or agent influences its surrounding knowledge environment.

nodes.label: GARDEN_GUIDELINES
nodes.description: The vault-level rules for publishing notes to the public garden and maintaining overall knowledge hygiene.
